name: hyx
desc: Powerful hex editor for the console
why: A console hex editor with a strong feature set; a solid binary-poking tool, though hex editors are a crowded niche.

brief.what_it_is: hyx is a terminal hex editor written in C. The homepage describes it as a minimalistic (under 2500 lines of C) but powerful editor with hex and ASCII views, insert, replace and delete, copy and paste, undo and redo, search, colors, and vim-inspired controls. It opens a binary file and lets you edit its bytes in the console. The homepage gives no details on file formats or output beyond the edited file itself.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage lists hyx as a tool under the author's 'tools' section, alongside ynetd, and gives no explicit problem statement. Its framing is simply a small, powerful console hex editor.
brief.install_notes: The package is installed with brew install hyx and provides a single executable named hyx. I did not read a README or docs page, so I found no first-run steps, configuration, or runtime requirements beyond that.
brief.standout: It is aimed at being very small, under 2500 lines of C, while still offering insert, copy/paste, undo/redo, and search. The vim-inspired controls are a deliberate choice for people who already know vim. The scout notes call it a strong feature set in a crowded niche of hex editors.
brief.status: Maintained, by the homepage's own listing: it shows hyx at version 2026.01.11, which is recent relative to the other tools listed (the newest ones date from 2025 and 2026). I could not check a commit history or release page, so I cannot confirm a last commit date.
brief.caveats: I only read the author's index page, not a dedicated hyx page or source repository, so I could not confirm supported platforms, license, or the exact key bindings. The homepage text I received did not expose hyperlink URLs, so no separate docs link is listed. The scout notes say hex editors are a crowded niche.
